chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn 'Amr al-Yamani, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds,' he said: 'The night prayer of the believer removes what he committed of sin during the day.'

key_terms.إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَ: Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds (Quranic verse)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ بِاللَّيْلِ: The night prayer of the believer

ai.seo_question: How does night prayer expiate daytime sins according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the general principle of 'good deeds removing bad deeds' is specifically applied to the night prayer, highlighting its unique efficacy in expiating daytime sins. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on Salat al-Layl as a primary means of spiritual purification and divine forgiveness, linking ritual devotion directly to moral accountability.
